examples.en: I steep tea in hot water.
Yesterday I made broth by simmering dried anchovies.

examples.ko: 티백을 너무 오래 우리면 쓴맛이 나요.
examples.en: If you steep a tea bag too long, it tastes bitter.
I drank the barley tea my grandmother brewed.
I'm going to cold-brew green tea.
After simmering the beef bones for a long time, the broth turned white.

explain: 차나 국물처럼 재료의 맛과 색을 물에 내는 일에 써요. 재료가 주어가 아니라 목적어예요: '차를 우리다'. 같은 그림에서 재료 쪽을 말하면 '우러나다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when you draw the flavor and color of an ingredient into water, as with tea or broth. The ingredient is the object: '차를 우리다'. From the ingredient's side, say '우러나다' (the flavor comes out).

examples.en: I think so too.
It was like that in the past, too.
Everyone has times like that.
It will be the same from now on.
Because that was the situation, nobody objected.
It's always like that during exam season, isn't it?

explain: 말할 때는 '그래요', '그렇다'를 더 많이 써요. '그러하다'는 글이나 격식 있는 말에서 보여요. '그러한'과 '그러해서'는 '그런', '그래서'로 줄여 말하는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: In everyday speech '그래요' and '그렇다' are more common. 그러하다 shows up in writing and formal speech. '그러한' and '그러해서' are often shortened to '그런' and '그래서' in conversation.

examples.en: Korean food is represented by kimchi.

examples.ko: 그 시대는 이 노래 한 곡으로 대표되었어요.
examples.en: That era was represented by this one song.
Our class was represented by Minsu.

examples.ko: 서울은 높은 빌딩으로 대표될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Seoul can be represented by its tall buildings.
I learn about traditional culture represented by the hanbok.
That singer is known as a representative of ballads.

explain: '대표하다'는 앞장서서 대표가 되는 것이고, '대표되다'는 전체가 어떤 것으로 대표된다는 말이에요. 'A로 대표되다'처럼 '로' 앞에 전체를 보여 주는 대표를 써요. 주어는 대표를 받는 쪽(한국 음식, 이 도시)이에요.
explain_en: '대표하다' means someone stands as the representative. 대표되다 means a whole group or idea is represented by one thing: 'A로 대표되다' (be represented by A). The subject is the whole being represented, such as Korean food or a city.

examples.en: The teacher gets every student involved in class.
We got the kids to take part in cleaning.
I want to involve the employees in the meeting.
If you involve guests in the event, they enjoy it more.
An event that involved the residents was held.
Don't force your younger sibling to join.

explain: 내가 참여하는 게 아니라 다른 사람이 참여하게 만들 때 써요. '참여하다'는 내가 하는 것, '참여시키다'는 상대를 끌어들이는 것이에요. 목적어에는 '을/를', 행사나 활동에는 '에'를 써요.
explain_en: Use this when you make someone else take part, not when you take part yourself. '참여하다' is what you do on your own; 참여시키다 brings someone else in. The person takes 을/를, and the event or activity takes 에.

en: such; of this kind; of this sort

examples.en: The situation is like this, so it can't be helped.
This is my situation, so please understand.
The results are as follows.
This kind of thing is a first for me.
The story went roughly like this.
If the plan is like this, I agree.

explain: 말할 때는 '이래요', '이런'을 더 많이 써요. '이러하다'는 발표나 글에서 '내용은 이러합니다'처럼 뒤에 나올 내용을 소개할 때 자주 보여요. '그러하다', '저러하다'와 짝이에요.
explain_en: In conversation, '이래요' and '이런' are used more. 이러하다 often appears in presentations and writing to introduce what comes next, as in '내용은 이러합니다'. It pairs with 그러하다 and 저러하다.

examples.en: This movie was produced in Korea.
A new drama will be produced next year.
It's an expensive bag because it's handmade.

examples.ko: 광고는 한 달 동안 제작될 거예요.
examples.en: The ad will be produced over a month.
The posters are being made.
These dolls are not made in a factory.

explain: 영화, 드라마, 광고, 포스터처럼 계획해서 만드는 결과물에 잘 써요. 일상의 음식이나 물건에는 '만들어지다'가 더 자연스러워요. 만드는 사람이 주어이면 '제작하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Good for planned works such as films, dramas, ads and posters. For everyday food and objects, '만들어지다' sounds more natural. If the maker is the subject, use '제작하다'.

examples.en: This disease has been studied for a long time.
A new method is being researched.
Korean language education is studied at many universities.
It hasn't been studied enough yet.
It's a field that will be researched more in the future.
It's a well-researched topic, so there are many sources.

explain: 연구의 대상이 되는 주제나 분야가 주어예요. '연구하다'는 사람이 하는 일, '연구되다'는 주제 쪽에서 말해요. 논문이나 뉴스에서 '연구되고 있다', '연구되지 않았다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: The subject is the topic or field being studied. '연구하다' has a person doing the research, while 연구되다 speaks from the topic's side. In papers and news you often see '연구되고 있다' and '연구되지 않았다'.

examples.en: This work is related to my major.
I saw news related to the accident.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 이 일과 관련되지 않았어요.
examples.en: That person isn't connected to this matter.
This document is related to taxes.
Please bring all the relevant documents.

examples.ko: 두 사건이 서로 관련됐을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: The two incidents may be related to each other.

explain: 'A와 관련되다' 또는 'A에 관련되다'로 써요. '관련이 있다'와 뜻이 가까운데, '관련되다'는 앞에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 '관련된 자료'처럼 자주 써요. 뉴스와 회사 말에서 흔해요.
explain_en: Used as 'A와 관련되다' or 'A에 관련되다' (be related to A). It is close to '관련이 있다', but 관련되다 is especially common as a modifier, as in '관련된 자료'. It is frequent in news and workplace language.

examples.en: The teacher made a song to help us remember the words.
This ad makes you remember the brand name.
I got my child to memorize our home address.

examples.ko: 부모님은 어릴 때부터 제 이름과 전화번호를 기억시키셨어요.
examples.en: My parents made me remember my name and phone number from when I was little.
We need to make the staff remember the safety rules.

examples.ko: 시험 날짜를 학생들에게 기억시키는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good to make students remember the exam date.

explain: 다른 사람이 기억하게 만든다는 말이에요. 비슷한 상황에서 한국 사람들은 '알려 주다', '상기시키다', '외우게 하다'도 써요. '기억하다'가 내가 기억하는 것이라면 이 말은 상대를 향해요.
explain_en: It means causing another person to remember something. In similar situations Koreans also use '알려 주다' (let someone know), '상기시키다' (remind) and '외우게 하다' (make someone memorize). '기억하다' is what you do yourself, while 기억시키다 is directed at someone else.

examples.en: This book is sold at bookstores nationwide.

examples.ko: 새 휴대폰은 다음 주부터 판매될 거예요.
examples.en: The new phone will go on sale next week.
Clothes sold online are cheaper.
This snack isn't sold anymore.
A hundred were sold in one day.

examples.ko: 그 가게에서 판매되고 있는 빵을 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried the bread being sold at that shop.

explain: 가게나 회사가 아니라 상품을 주어로 말할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '팔리다'도 많이 써요. '판매되다'는 상품 안내나 뉴스에 더 어울리고, '팔리다'는 '잘 팔려요'처럼 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It makes the product the subject instead of the shop or company. In daily speech '팔리다' is also common, as in '잘 팔려요' (it sells well). 판매되다 fits product notices and news better.

examples.en: This restaurant is often recommended in reviews.
Minsu was nominated as the representative.
It's a book recommended for beginners.

examples.ko: 이 방법은 더 이상 추천되지 않아요.
examples.en: This method is no longer recommended.
You will be put forward as a good candidate.
I took a cold medicine that many people recommend.

explain: 물건이나 방법이 주어이면 '사람들에게 권해진다'는 뜻이고, 사람이 주어이면 '후보로 올려진다'는 뜻이에요. 내가 권할 때는 '추천하다'를 써요. 추천받는 사람은 '에게', 추천한 쪽은 '에 의해'로 나타내요.
explain_en: With an item or method as the subject, it means people recommend it. With a person as the subject, it means being put forward as a candidate. When you are the one recommending, use '추천하다'. The person it is recommended to takes 에게, and the recommender takes 에 의해.

examples.en: We formed a team of five.
Let's first plan out the content of the presentation.
I'll divide the class into two groups.
It's a picture made up of several colors.

examples.ko: 수업을 재미있게 구성하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to design a class to be fun.
After setting up the group, we decided on rules.

explain: 여러 부분을 모아 하나의 체계를 만들 때 써요. '팀을 구성하다', '내용을 구성하다'처럼 사람과 내용 모두에 쓸 수 있어요. 구성되는 쪽을 주어로 하면 '구성되다'가 돼요.
explain_en: Used when you put several parts together into one organized whole. It works for both people and content, as in building a team or structuring content. When the whole is the subject, use '구성되다'.

examples.ko: 저는 이 사업을 꼭 성공시킬 거예요.
examples.en: I will definitely make this business a success.
The team members made the project a success.
I worked all night to make the experiment succeed.
What's the secret to making a small shop succeed?
Everyone works hard to make the plan succeed.
If you pull off the event, you get a bonus.

explain: '성공하다'는 일이 잘 되는 것이고, '성공시키다'는 내가 노력해서 일을 성공하게 만드는 것이에요. 목적어에 일, 사업, 계획 같은 것이 와요. 사람 자신이 목적어로 오는 말은 아니에요.
explain_en: '성공하다' means something goes well. 성공시키다 means you make an effort so that a task succeeds. The object is a thing like a project, business or plan, not the person themself.

examples.en: A new menu item was added.
The name wasn't added to the list.
If you order, a shipping fee is added.
A new feature will be added to the app.
I marked the added content in yellow.
One more assignment got added, so it's tough.

explain: 이미 있는 것에 더해진다는 말이에요. 반대로 빠지는 것은 '삭제되다', '제외되다'를 써요. 직접 더할 때는 '추가하다'예요. 돈이 더 붙을 때는 '비용이 추가되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means something is added on top of what already exists. The opposite, for things taken out, is '삭제되다' or '제외되다'. When you add something yourself, use '추가하다'. Extra costs are also described with this verb: '비용이 추가되다'.

examples.en: This park is managed by the city hall.
Personal information is being kept safe.
A well-kept garden is really pretty.
The records weren't properly maintained.
From now on, the inventory will be managed separately.
Even though the building is old, it's good that it's kept clean.

explain: 사람이 아니라 건물, 정보, 재고처럼 관리의 대상이 주어일 때 써요. 누가 관리하는지 밝힐 때는 '에 의해'를 써요. 건강이나 피부는 보통 '관리하다'를 쓰고 '관리되다'로는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: The subject is the thing being looked after, such as a building, data or stock, not a person. The one who manages it is marked with '에 의해'. Talk about your own health or skin usually uses '관리하다' instead of 관리되다.

examples.en: I installed an air conditioner at home.
I install a new app on my phone.

examples.ko: 내일 기사님이 와서 인터넷을 설치할 거예요.
examples.en: Tomorrow a technician will come and set up the internet.
It takes about thirty minutes to install.
After installing the program, I turned off the computer.
A fire extinguisher must be installed in this building.

explain: 앱과 프로그램, 에어컨, 카메라 같은 기계를 자리에 놓고 쓸 수 있게 할 때 써요. 앱은 '설치하다'로 받고, 지울 때는 '삭제하다'를 써요. 짝말은 '설치되다'예요.
explain_en: Used for apps and programs as well as machines like air conditioners and cameras, when you put them in place so they can be used. For apps, the opposite is '삭제하다' (delete). The passive partner is '설치되다'.

examples.en: This plan isn't complete yet.
Please answer in a complete sentence.

examples.ko: 그 설명은 완전해서 더 물어볼 게 없어요.
examples.en: The explanation is complete, so there is nothing more to ask.
No one can be perfect.
I check that the door is fully closed.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 선수가 다 모여서 완전해졌어요.
examples.en: The team became complete once all the players gathered.

explain: 빠진 것 없이 다 갖춰진 상태예요. 일상 대화에서는 부사 '완전'이 '완전 맛있어요'처럼 '아주'와 비슷하게 쓰여요. 이때는 '완전하다'로 활용하지 않고 '완전' 그대로 써요.
explain_en: It describes a state where nothing is missing. In casual conversation the adverb '완전' is used like 'totally' or 'very', as in '완전 맛있어요'. In that use it does not conjugate; you say 완전, not 완전하다.

examples.en: Please do the homework a bit faster.

examples.ko: 저는 일을 빨리해야 퇴근할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can leave work only if I get things done quickly.

examples.ko: 준비를 빨리하면 일찍 출발할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get ready quickly, we can leave early.
I did the dishes quickly and then rested.
I'm trying to make decisions quickly.
I tend to wash my face quickly in the morning.

explain: '일을 빨리하다'처럼 동작을 서두를 때 써요. '빨리 하다'로 띄어 쓰기도 해요. 말할 때는 '빨리 가다', '빨리 먹다'처럼 부사 '빨리'를 다른 동사 앞에 붙이는 일이 더 많고, 재촉할 때는 '빨리빨리', '서둘러 주세요'를 자주 써요.
explain_en: Used when you hurry an action, like doing a task quickly. It can also be written with a space: '빨리 하다'. In speech, people more often put the adverb 빨리 before another verb, as in '빨리 가다' and '빨리 먹다'. To urge someone, '빨리빨리' and '서둘러 주세요' are very common.

examples.en: This shop gives a drink for free.
The owner gave us dessert on the house.
The company plans to offer service in Korean, too.
The new app will be offered starting next month.
Many shops give things to customers for free.
The game that had run for a long time ended this year.

explain: 한국에서 '서비스'는 가게에서 덤으로 주는 것이라는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. '서비스로 주세요'처럼 말해요. 그래서 '서비스하다'도 공짜로 주는 것이나 앱, 게임을 제공하는 것을 말해요.
explain_en: In Korea, '서비스' is also commonly used for a free extra a shop gives you, as in '서비스로 주세요'. So 서비스하다 can mean giving something free or running an app or game for users.

en: be expressed; be represented; be manifested

examples.en: That feeling is well expressed in the song.
Sadness was expressed in the painting.
This word is hard to express in English.
The season depicted in the poem is autumn.
Emotions show up on the face as they are.

examples.ko: 숫자로 표현될 수 없는 가치도 있어요.
examples.en: There are also values that can't be expressed in numbers.

explain: 감정이나 생각이 말, 그림, 얼굴 등으로 드러난다는 말이에요. '표현하다'는 내가 나타내는 것이고, '표현되다'는 감정이 주어로 나와요. 어디에 나타나는지는 '에/으로'로 말해요.
explain_en: It means a feeling or thought shows through words, pictures or a face. '표현하다' has you expressing something, while with 표현되다 the feeling itself is the subject. '에' or '(으)로' marks where it appears.

en: apply to; be applicable; fall under

examples.en: This rule applies to every student.
It doesn't apply in my case.
Please mark the box that applies.
Children are eligible for this discount.
Only those it applies to should submit the form.

examples.ko: 이 조건에 해당될 때 연락 주세요.
examples.en: Please contact me if you meet this condition.

explain: 조건이나 규칙에 맞아서 적용된다는 뜻이에요. 서류에서 '해당 사항 없음'처럼 자주 보여요. '해당되는 것에 표시하세요'처럼 쓰고, 어떤 사람에게 적용되는지는 '에게'로 말해요.
explain_en: It means a condition or rule fits a case and so applies. It appears often on forms in the phrase '해당 사항 없음' (not applicable). The person it applies to is marked with '에게'.

examples.en: The meeting is scheduled for tomorrow afternoon.
It ended earlier than the scheduled time.

examples.ko: 수리가 다음 주로 예정되어서 가게를 쉴 거예요.
examples.en: The repairs are scheduled for next week, so the shop will be closed.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 올가을에 개봉하는 것으로 예정됐어요.
examples.en: That movie is slated to open this fall.

examples.ko: 새 건물의 완공은 내년으로 예정되어 있어요.
examples.en: The new building is scheduled to be completed next year.
Two performances were scheduled.

explain: 일이 앞으로 있을 것으로 정해져 있다는 말이에요. 보통 '예정되어 있다'로 쓰고, '예정이다'와 거의 같게 쓰여요. 사람이 주어일 때는 '~할 예정이에요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It says something is already set to happen in the future. It is usually used as '예정되어 있다' and works almost like '예정이다'. When a person is the subject, '~할 예정이에요' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 저희는 다음 주에 여행을 예정하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are planning a trip next week.
I scheduled the meeting for Friday.
I will set the show for three p.m.
They're a couple planning to marry next year.
I planned my vacation for August, so I bought a plane ticket.

examples.ko: 예정한 날짜를 바꿔야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think we have to change the planned date.

explain: 말할 때는 '계획하다'나 '~할 예정이에요'를 더 자주 써요. '예정하다'는 날짜와 시간이 정해진 일에 어울려서 공지, 뉴스에서 보여요. 막연한 생각에는 '생각 중이에요'를 써요.
explain_en: In speech, '계획하다' and '~할 예정이에요' are used more. 예정하다 suits events with a set date or time and shows up in notices and news. For a vague idea, say '생각 중이에요' (I'm thinking about it).

examples.en: Such opinions keep being put forward.
This theory was proposed long ago.
Let's check whether what is being claimed is true.
A new rule is being advocated among students.

examples.ko: 그의 말은 증거 없이 주장된 거예요.
examples.en: His words were claimed without evidence.
These ideas will keep being claimed in the future.

explain: '내가 주장하다'가 아니라 어떤 의견이 주장되고 있다는 말이에요. 뉴스, 논문, 토론에서 주로 써요. 일상에서는 '말하다', '우기다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '우기다'는 고집을 부린다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Instead of 'I insist', this describes an opinion being put forward. It is mainly used in news, papers and debates. In daily life '말하다' and '우기다' are more common; 우기다 suggests stubbornness.

examples.en: The teacher proctors the exam.
That person directed the movie.
I work supervising a construction site.

examples.ko: 부모님이 숙제를 감독하면 아이가 더 열심히 해요.
examples.en: When parents keep an eye on homework, kids work harder.
Tomorrow I'll oversee it myself.

examples.ko: 축구팀을 감독한 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It's been five years since I started coaching the soccer team.

explain: 사람이나 일이 규칙대로 되는지 지켜보고 이끄는 일이에요. 영화에서는 '영화를 감독하다', 운동에서는 팀을 이끄는 사람을 '감독'이라고 불러요. 사람을 부를 때는 '감독님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means watching and guiding people or work to see that things go by the rules. For films it means directing. In sports the head of a team is called a '감독'. When addressing the person, say '감독님'.

examples.en: A firefighter rescued the child.
They rescue people who fell into the sea.

examples.ko: 산에서 길을 잃은 사람들을 구조할 거예요.
examples.en: They will rescue the people lost in the mountains.
The rescue took two hours.
I have rescued a stray dog before.

examples.ko: 다친 사람들을 무사히 구조해 줘서 고마워요.
examples.en: Thank you for rescuing the injured people safely.

explain: 위험에 빠진 사람이나 동물을 도와서 벗어나게 할 때 써요. '도와주다'는 일상의 도움이고, '구조하다'는 사고나 재난처럼 위험한 상황에 써요. 구조받는 쪽은 '구조되다'예요.
explain_en: Used when you help a person or animal escape danger. '도와주다' covers everyday help, while 구조하다 is for accidents and disasters. The one rescued uses '구조되다'.

examples.en: The meeting time was changed.
I got a text saying my password was changed.
The schedule might change suddenly.
Please send it to the updated address.
The reservation wasn't changed.
The rule changed, so I'll explain it again.

explain: 일정, 시간, 주소처럼 정해진 내용이 다른 것으로 바뀔 때 써요. 공지나 문자에서 자주 봐요. 자연스럽게 모습이 달라지는 변화에는 '변하다'를 쓰고, 이 말은 정한 것을 바꾼다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Used when a fixed detail such as a schedule, time or address is switched to something else. You often see it in notices and text messages. For a natural change in appearance or state, a different verb is used, while this one suggests a set arrangement was altered.

examples.en: A new club was formed.
This group is made up of students.
It's a well-organized team, so work is quick.
A committee will be formed for the event.
The residents gathered, and a village group was formed.
The team hasn't been properly organized yet.

explain: 사람들이 모여서 역할을 나누고 하나의 단체가 만들어질 때 써요. '단체가 조직되다'처럼 단체가 주어예요. 만드는 사람이 주어이면 '조직하다'예요. '구성되다'는 어떤 부분으로 이루어졌는지에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: Used when people gather, split roles and a group takes shape, so the group is the subject. If the founder is the subject, the active form is used. A near neighbor, 'be composed', focuses more on which parts make up the whole.

examples.en: This film is rated as a good work.
My ability was assessed by the test score.
That player is regarded as the best.
I was upset because I wasn't judged fairly.
It's a highly rated book, so give it a read.
It may be reassessed later.

explain: '좋다', '나쁘다'처럼 다른 사람에게 점수나 가치가 매겨진다는 말이에요. 'A로 평가되다'의 틀이 많아요. 내가 직접 평가하면 '평가하다'를 쓰고, 칭찬이면 '높이 평가하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a person or thing is given a value or score by others. It is often used in the pattern 'is rated as A'. When you judge something yourself, the active verb is used, and for praise people say they rate something highly.

examples.en: This app works like a map.

examples.ko: 약이 제대로 기능하지 않는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The medicine doesn't seem to be working properly.
That room also served as a study.

examples.ko: 몸의 모든 부분이 함께 기능하는 거예요.
examples.en: All parts of the body function together.
This rule will serve as a guide.
The system is functioning well, so there's no problem.

explain: 기계의 작동보다는 어떤 것이 맡은 역할을 한다는 뜻에서 자주 써요. 'A로 기능하다'는 'A 역할을 하다'와 같아요. 기계가 움직인다고 할 때는 '작동하다', '돌아가다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used more for something playing its role than for a machine running. 'Function as A' means to act in the role of A. For machines simply running, other verbs meaning 'operate' or 'run' are more common.

examples.en: Walking alone on a night road feels dangerous.
Don't play risky pranks.
The child was sitting on the railing, which looked dangerous.
The driving felt dangerous.

examples.ko: 그 계획은 조금 위험스러울 것 같아요.
examples.en: That plan seems a bit risky.
It looked dangerous, so I didn't go near it.

explain: '위험하다'는 사실로 위험한 것, '위험스럽다'는 위험해 보이거나 그렇게 느껴진다는 말이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '위험스러워요', '위험스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 말할 때는 '위험해 보여요'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: The plain adjective states that something is actually dangerous, while this one says it looks or feels dangerous. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so the ending changes in forms like the polite present and the modifier. In speech, 'it looks dangerous' is also common.

examples.en: Our company will be relocated next month.
The hospital was moved downtown.
The school is planned to move to a new building.
The new address is on the website.
The data is being transferred to the server.
The rights haven't been transferred yet.

explain: 사무실, 병원, 학교처럼 있던 곳이 다른 곳으로 옮겨질 때 써요. 이사한다는 뜻의 '이사하다'는 집에 쓰고, 이 말은 기관이나 자료에 어울려요. '이전'은 '지난'이라는 뜻의 다른 낱말도 있어요.
explain_en: Used when an office, hospital or school moves from one place to another. The everyday verb for moving house is for homes, while this one fits institutions and data. Note that the same sound can also be a different word meaning 'before'.

examples.en: The company moved to Gangnam.
Our shop is relocating next week.
We plan to relocate the office.
I'm moving the files to a new computer.
After moving, the address changed.
Relocating a school takes a lot of time.

explain: 회사나 가게, 학교 같은 곳이 자리를 옮기는 걸 말해요. 개인이 집을 옮길 때는 '이사하다'를 써요. 짝말은 '이전되다'이고, 주어가 직접 옮기면 '이전하다', 옮겨지는 쪽이면 '이전되다'예요.
explain_en: Used when a company, shop or school changes its location. For a person moving house, a different everyday verb is used. Its passive partner is used when the place is moved, while this active form is used when the subject moves itself.

examples.en: This material was referred to in the report.
Your opinions will be taken into account.
The book that was consulted is in the library.
This will be considered in the review.

examples.ko: 이 문서가 참고되고 있는지 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check whether this document is being referred to.
The old records weren't consulted.

explain: 자료나 의견이 판단하거나 결정할 때 도움으로 쓰인다는 말이에요. 내가 볼 때는 '참고하다'를 써요. '참고로 말씀드리면'은 덧붙여 알려 줄 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
explain_en: It means a source or opinion is used as an aid when judging or deciding. When you are the one consulting, the active verb is used. A related phrase, 'for your reference', is used to add extra information.

examples.en: These two are the most important.
Please summarize only the main points.
I do the less important things later.

examples.ko: 이 부분이 주요해서 꼭 외워야 해요.
examples.en: This part is key, so you must memorize it.
The main reason was the price.
It's a technology that will become more important.

explain: '주요하다' 자체는 글에서 쓰고, 말할 때는 뒤에 명사가 오는 '주요 뉴스', '주요 내용'이 더 흔해요. '중요하다'는 사람이나 일이 소중하다는 느낌, '주요하다'는 여럿 중 중심이 되는 것에 어울려요.
explain_en: The adjective itself is mostly written, and in speech the noun-modifying use, like 'main news' or 'main points', is more common. The word for 'important' suggests something matters to you, while this one fits the central items among many.

examples.en: The city holds a festival every year.
Do you know the country that hosted the Olympics?
The school will hold a sports day in autumn.
There's a lot to prepare to host a competition.
After holding the exhibition, it became very popular.
We held a small concert.

explain: 축제, 대회, 전시회 같은 큰 행사를 여는 주최자가 쓰는 말이에요. 작은 모임이나 파티에는 '열다'나 '하다'가 자연스러워요. 열리는 행사를 주어로 하면 '개최되다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used by an organizer for big events such as festivals, contests and exhibitions. For small gatherings and parties, the plain verbs for 'open' or 'do' sound natural. When the event is the subject, the passive form is used.

examples.en: This factory produces cars.
The farmers produced rice.
This year they'll produce a lot of apples.
There are several ways to produce electricity.
I bought a product made in Korea.
We're producing a thousand a day.

explain: 공장이나 농장에서 물건을 만들어 낼 때 써요. 파는 쪽의 '판매하다', 사는 쪽의 '소비하다'와 한 묶음으로 자주 나와요. 개인이 만든 작은 물건에는 '만들다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Used when a factory or farm turns out goods. It often appears in a set with the verb for selling and the one for consuming. For small things an individual makes, the plain verb for 'make' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The file was moved to another folder.
The luggage is moved onto the truck.
The patient is being taken to the hospital.
Let's restart from the new position.

examples.ko: 사진이 다른 곳으로 이동될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: The photos may be moved elsewhere.
The desk has been moved to the window.

explain: 사람이 걸어가는 게 아니라 물건, 자료, 환자처럼 다른 힘으로 옮겨질 때 써요. 내가 직접 가는 건 '이동하다'를 써요. 컴퓨터에서 파일을 옮겼다고 할 때도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Used when things like objects, data or a patient are moved by some other force, not when a person walks. When you go by yourself, the active verb is used. It also comes up often for files being moved on a computer.

examples.en: I move the luggage to the warehouse.
A staff member moved the patient to the bed.
Please move the car somewhere else.
You can move the photo with the mouse.
We're moving the students to the classroom.
I moved the chairs and cleaned.

explain: 사람이나 물건을 다른 곳으로 옮기게 한다는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '옮기다'가 훨씬 자주 쓰이고, 이 말은 안내문이나 설명서처럼 딱딱한 글에서 보여요. 목적어가 필요해요.
explain_en: It means causing a person or object to move elsewhere. In daily life, the plain native verb for 'move' is far more common, and this one shows up in notices and manuals. It always takes an object.

examples.en: The teacher guides the students' presentations.
I coached the juniors in the club.
The teacher who coaches exercise has come.
I'm grateful to the professor who advises my thesis.
You need patience when guiding children.
I have experience guiding students for a long time.

explain: 가르치고 이끄는 일이에요. '가르치다'는 지식을 전하는 것이고, '지도하다'는 방향을 잡아 주고 도와주는 느낌이 강해요. 명사 '지도'는 'map'과 소리가 같아서 문맥으로 구별해야 해요.
explain_en: It means teaching and leading. The plain verb for 'teach' passes on knowledge, while this one stresses setting a direction and helping along. The noun form sounds the same as the word for a map, so context tells them apart.

examples.en: I work at home at night.
I went to bed late working on a video yesterday.
I'm in the middle of working on the design.
The friend I worked with helped me.

examples.ko: 조용한 카페에서 작업하면 집중이 잘 돼요.
examples.en: I focus well when working in a quiet cafe.
I'll work on this drawing until tomorrow.

explain: 공부나 사무가 아니라 그림, 영상, 음악, 사진처럼 만드는 결과물이 있는 일에 잘 써요. 회사 일 전반은 '일하다'가 자연스러워요. '작업'은 '작업 중'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It fits work that yields something you make, like pictures, videos, music or photos, not studying or office tasks. For jobs in general, the plain verb for 'work' sounds more natural. The noun form is also used often, as in 'in progress'.

examples.en: The city is changing quickly.
My way of thinking changed.
Language changes with the times.
I was surprised to see the changed look.
The environment will change a lot in the future.

examples.ko: 이 약을 먹은 뒤로 몸이 변화되지 않았어요.
examples.en: My body hasn't changed since I took this medicine.

explain: 시간이 지나면서 모습이나 상태가 달라진다는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '변하다', '달라지다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '변화되다'는 글이나 발표에서 큰 흐름의 변화를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It means appearance or state differs as time passes. In daily life, the plain verbs for 'change' and 'become different' sound much more natural. This longer passive is used in writing and presentations for larger trends.
